# Jim's project knowledge base

Personal data. This file is gitignored. Agents may use only facts written here (plus the CV) when rewriting.
Where two versions of a fact exist, both are listed and marked TO CONFIRM.

## AI-Powered Review Response System
category: work
employer: JudgeService Research Ltd
period: Jan 2024 to Present
problem: UK car dealerships receive large volumes of customer reviews and struggle to reply quickly, consistently and within each dealer group's wording rules.
built: An LLM service that drafts three reply options for every customer review (detailed, professional, short) using sentiment-conditioned prompts with per-dealership rules baked in; the dealer picks one and publishes. Fine-tuned Llama 3 8B with LoRA/QLoRA (Unsloth) on examples generated by a 70B model, distilling its ability to follow strict client wording rules that the base model could not manage, while keeping small-model speed and cost. Deployed on AWS EC2, configuring NVIDIA drivers and the Linux environment from scratch, then led the migration to an on-prem GPU server and added database-level caching of repeat requests to cut costs and response times. Live across major UK dealer groups.
stack: Python, Llama 3 8B, LoRA, QLoRA, Unsloth, Llama 3 70B, AWS EC2, NVIDIA drivers, Linux, on-prem GPU server, database caching, prompt engineering, FastAPI, Docker
metrics: 93% of drafts published unedited, 100k reviews/month, 3 reply options per review, 8B model distilled from 70B
keywords: LLM service, fine-tuning, distillation, sentiment-conditioned prompts, GPU serving, migration to on-prem, caching, production LLM, dealer groups

## Customer Insight AI Agent & Sentiment Platform
category: work
employer: JudgeService Research Ltd
period: Jan 2024 to Present
problem: Clients needed structured, per-topic insight from thousands of raw reviews to drive dashboards, complaint handling and account-management conversations.
built: A multi-agent NLP/LLM pipeline that parses every incoming review into structured JSON: review-type classification, per-topic sentiment, supporting evidence quotes and staff-name linking/recognition, feeding the dashboards clients use for reporting and the company's complaint-handling platform. Raised subcategory recall from 0.78 to 0.96 (F1 0.98) on a golden set of hard cases (500 reviews per CV, 1,500 reviews per alternate version, TO CONFIRM), then locked in the gains with a CI regression gate that re-runs the set on every change and fails the build if accuracy drops. Two-tier / hybrid routing: urgent single reviews go to the Gemini API for low latency while bulk batch jobs run on a self-hosted open-weights model (Gemma 27B per CV, Gemma 4 31B per alternate version, TO CONFIRM) on the company's own GPU hardware, cutting per-review cost with no vendor lock-in. Consolidated six task-specific models across two products into one self-hosted model, scaling throughput 2x on the same 48 GB GPU and recovering 10+ GB of VRAM to run batch jobs, agents and both applications concurrently. Designed a zero-downtime serving layer: active-passive Ollama servers behind HAProxy with automatic failover. Adopted by account managers to prepare for client meetings: per-dealer breakdowns show where a dealership is struggling before the team walks in, sharpening renewal and upsell conversations.
stack: Python, multi-agent pipeline, Gemini API, Gemma 27B, Gemma 4 31B, Ollama, HAProxy, 48 GB GPU, structured JSON output, CI regression gate, golden dataset, MLOps, NLP, sentiment analysis, classification, evaluation
metrics: 20% lift in client retention, recall 0.78 to 0.96, F1 0.98, 500-review golden set, 1,500-review golden dataset, 2x throughput, 48 GB GPU, 10+ GB VRAM recovered, six models consolidated into one, two products
keywords: multi-agent, sentiment, structured extraction, evaluation, golden set, regression gate, MLOps, hybrid routing, self-hosted open-weights, cost optimisation, zero-downtime, failover, client dashboards, retention

## RAG Documentation Engine, QA Automation & Mentoring
category: work
employer: JudgeService Research Ltd
period: Jan 2024 to Present
problem: Legacy PHP/JS codebases were undocumented and the code could not leave company infrastructure; call-quality QA audits were manual; the development team needed to adopt AI tooling.
built: A privacy-first RAG pipeline that documents legacy PHP/JS codebases with no code leaving company infrastructure: LangChain ingestion, 2,000-character chunking, Linq-Embed-Mistral embeddings in a local Chroma store, and Llama 3 via Ollama; retrieval surrounds each chunk with related cross-file context. An automated call-quality assessment tool using WhisperX transcription (speech-to-text) and rule-based LLM analysis, replacing manual QA audits. Internal workshops on LLM capabilities and prompt engineering that accelerated adoption of AI tooling across the development team.
stack: LangChain, Chroma, Linq-Embed-Mistral, Llama 3, Ollama, WhisperX, speech-to-text, RAG, embeddings, chunking, PHP, JavaScript, prompt engineering
metrics: 90% reduction in manual documentation work, 2,000-character chunks
keywords: RAG, privacy-first, local embeddings, vector store, documentation automation, STT, QA automation, mentoring, workshops, prompt engineering
